title: Granz's first jam sessions in Los Angeles
summary: Granz ran small sessions in L.A. paying $9; Young, Willie Smith, Nat Cole and Red Callender played, and Granz later paid well and traveled first class.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Yes, she has. You know, when we met

Norman, he was just running little jazz sessions out at the True Building. He's giving -- he'd give us (unintelligible) come into L.A. And he just finished UCLA, and when we'd come in L.A. he would try to run these sessions. And he'd give us $9.00 to go out there. And he had the money to play these little things out there at Trueville and little places like that. Willie Smith, Nat Cole, myself, Red Callender, we all used to go out and play them for him to help him out.
What -- do you remember what year that was?

Well, it'd have to be when I was with Lunceford, so that would be between '37 and -- it would be between '37 and '40 or '41. It had to be between there because that's -- those are the years I worked with Lunceford. And he was a good friend of Willie and (unintelligible) Fishelli, you know, because Norman didn't have a car then and Fishelli used to let him use their car. Sometime you talk to Fishelli about Norman. You'd learn.
It'd sure open up your eyes to a lot of things because -- we knew Norman when he had little patches on his britches and all around there. We knew him a long time ago.
Well, he doesn't dress too much better now. He just has (inaudible).
Yeah. He got the bread now, you know. He made a lot of money from the business.

But I'll give him this. The guy was first class. Yeah, he was first class in doing things, you know. I liked him for that because he was the first -- one of the first guys I knew that really started paying the musicians some money when he made it, some fairly decent money, you know. And he travelled first class all the time. He lived in the best hotels, and everything was first class.
